questions.question: During the preoperative assessment, which two patient identifiers are most appropriate for verifying patient identity before surgery?
choices: Full name and date of birth
questions.explanation: Acceptable identifiers must be specific to the individual and not change with location; full name and date of birth meet this standard, whereas room and bed numbers do not.

questions.question: A patient with well-controlled hypertension and no functional limitations presents for an elective procedure. Which ASA Physical Status classification is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: ASA II describes a patient with mild systemic disease without substantive functional limitations, such as well-controlled hypertension.

questions.question: The modified Aldrete score evaluates five parameters to assess PACU recovery. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: The modified Aldrete score assesses activity, respiration, circulation, consciousness, and oxygen saturation; urine output is not a component.

questions.question: The Universal Protocol for preventing wrong-site, wrong-procedure, and wrong-person surgery consists of which three principal components?
choices: Consent, anesthesia review, and discharge planning
Preprocedure verification, site marking, and time-out
questions.explanation: The Joint Commission Universal Protocol comprises a preprocedure verification process, marking of the operative site, and a time-out immediately before the procedure begins.

questions.question: The ASA Physical Status classification system was developed primarily to do what?
choices: Predict the exact duration of surgery
Assess and communicate a patient's preanesthetic comorbidity burden
questions.explanation: The ASA Physical Status system is a standardized assessment of preoperative systemic health to communicate comorbidity, not a direct predictor of surgical risk alone.

questions.question: A PACU patient can move all four extremities voluntarily or on command. What Aldrete activity score does this earn?
questions.explanation: Moving all four extremities voluntarily or on command scores 2 on the Aldrete activity component.

questions.question: When marking the surgical site, who is responsible for placing the mark?
choices: The licensed practitioner who will perform the procedure
questions.explanation: The site should be marked by the licensed independent practitioner who is ultimately accountable for the procedure and, ideally, will be present at the time of surgery.

questions.question: A completely healthy, non-smoking patient with minimal alcohol use is scheduled for surgery. What is the correct ASA class?
questions.explanation: ASA I designates a normal healthy patient who does not smoke and uses little or no alcohol.

questions.question: On the modified Aldrete scale, a patient who can breathe deeply and cough freely scores how for respiration?
questions.explanation: The ability to breathe deeply and cough freely earns the maximum respiration score of 2.

questions.question: The surgical site mark should ideally be made using which method to ensure it remains visible after skin prep?
choices: A permanent surgical marker placed at or near the incision site
A temporary tattoo applied by the patient
An adhesive label near the site
questions.explanation: AORN recommends marking with a permanent marker at or adjacent to the planned incision so the mark remains visible after skin antisepsis.

questions.question: The 'E' modifier added to an ASA Physical Status classification indicates what?
choices: An emergency procedure where delay would increase threat to life or body part
The patient has an endocrine disorder
The patient is on extracorporeal support
questions.explanation: The E modifier denotes an emergency operation, defined as one in which delay would significantly increase the threat to life or a body part.

questions.question: In the modified Aldrete circulation component, which finding earns a score of 2?
choices: BP more than 50% from the preanesthetic level
BP within 20% of the preanesthetic level
BP 20% to 50% from the preanesthetic level
questions.explanation: The modified Aldrete circulation parameter is scored on percentage change from the preanesthetic baseline, not an absolute mmHg difference: within 20% scores 2, 20-50% scores 1, and more than 50% scores 0. The distinction changes the score - 20 mmHg below an 80 mmHg baseline is a 25% fall, which scores 1, not 2.

questions.question: A time-out must be performed at what point during the perioperative process?
choices: Upon arrival in the preoperative holding area
After the first incision is made
Immediately before the start of the procedure
questions.explanation: The time-out is conducted immediately before starting the procedure, with the entire surgical team actively participating before incision.

questions.question: A patient with severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life, such as a myocardial infarction within the past three months, is best classified as which ASA status?
questions.explanation: ASA IV describes severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life, such as a recent MI, CVA, or TIA within three months.

questions.question: A PACU patient maintains SpO2 above 92 percent on room air. What Aldrete oxygen saturation score applies?
questions.explanation: An SpO2 above 92 percent breathing room air earns the maximum oxygen saturation score of 2.

questions.question: Which element is NOT a required component of the surgical time-out?
choices: Estimated blood loss for the case
Availability of correct implants when applicable
questions.explanation: Estimated blood loss is documented intraoperatively and at closing, not as part of the pre-incision time-out, which confirms patient, procedure, site, position, and required equipment or implants.

questions.question: A moribund patient who is not expected to survive without the operation is classified as which ASA status?
questions.explanation: ASA V designates a moribund patient not expected to survive without the operation, such as a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.

questions.question: The Aldrete consciousness component awards a score of 2 when the patient is:
questions.explanation: Being fully awake earns the maximum consciousness score of 2; arousable on calling scores 1.

questions.question: Informed consent for a surgical procedure is primarily the responsibility of which team member?
questions.explanation: Obtaining informed consent, including disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternatives, is the legal and ethical responsibility of the operating surgeon.

questions.question: ASA Physical Status VI is reserved for which type of patient?
choices: A patient with end-stage renal disease on dialysis
A declared brain-dead patient whose organs are being removed for donation
A moribund patient undergoing emergency surgery
questions.explanation: ASA VI is assigned to a declared brain-dead patient whose organs are being removed for donor purposes.

questions.question: A commonly used minimum total modified Aldrete score for discharge from PACU phase I is:
questions.explanation: A total modified Aldrete score of 9 or greater (out of 10) is the commonly accepted threshold for phase I discharge readiness.

questions.question: What is the nurse's role regarding the informed consent document in the preoperative period?
choices: Explaining the surgical risks and alternatives in detail
Witnessing the patient's signature and verifying it is in the chart
Deciding whether the patient is a candidate for surgery
Determining the surgical approach to be used
questions.explanation: The nurse witnesses the signature and confirms the consent is signed, dated, and present; detailed disclosure of risks and alternatives is the surgeon's duty.

questions.question: A patient with poorly controlled diabetes, morbid obesity (BMI of 42), and active substance abuse but no immediate life threat is best classified as which ASA status?
questions.explanation: ASA III describes severe systemic disease with substantive functional limitations, including poorly controlled diabetes, morbid obesity, and active substance dependence.

questions.question: In the perioperative nursing process (ADPIE), which phase immediately follows assessment?
questions.explanation: The ADPIE sequence is Assessment, Nursing Diagnosis, Outcome identification/Planning, Implementation, and Evaluation; nursing diagnosis directly follows assessment.

questions.question: When individualizing the plan of care for a frail 84-year-old patient undergoing hip surgery, which age-related change most directly increases the risk of intraoperative hypothermia?
choices: Diminished thermoregulation and reduced muscle mass
questions.explanation: Older adults have diminished thermoregulatory control and reduced muscle mass, lowering their ability to generate and conserve heat. This warrants proactive warming measures in the plan of care.

questions.question: The AORN Perioperative Patient Focused Model is organized into how many domains?
questions.explanation: The PNDS Perioperative Patient Focused Model comprises four domains: Safety, Physiologic Responses, Behavioral Responses, and Health System.

questions.question: A pediatric patient who weighs 14 kg is scheduled for surgery. Why is individualizing the care plan by weight especially critical in this population?
choices: Medication and fluid dosing are weight-based, narrowing the safety margin
Children tolerate fluid overload better than adults
Pediatric patients have larger blood volumes per kg
Anesthetic agents have no pediatric considerations
questions.explanation: Pediatric medication and fluid dosing is calculated per kilogram, so small errors have proportionally larger effects. Weight-based individualization protects against overdose and fluid imbalance.

questions.question: An expected outcome stating the patient is 'free from signs and symptoms of infection' is classified under which PNDS domain?
questions.explanation: Freedom from signs and symptoms of infection falls under the Safety domain (D1) in the PNDS model, not Physiologic Responses.

questions.question: A patient states that family members must be present for major care decisions per their cultural traditions. The most appropriate nursing action is to:
choices: Document the preference and incorporate family in the plan as the patient wishes
Disregard the request to maintain efficiency
Refer the matter solely to the surgeon
Explain that only the patient may participate in decisions
questions.explanation: Culturally competent care respects the patient's decision-making structure and incorporates the family when the patient desires. This individualizes the plan to the patient's values.

questions.question: Which PNDS domain addresses thermoregulation and maintenance of normothermia?
questions.explanation: Thermoregulation and normothermia are part of the Physiologic Responses domain (D2), which also covers fluid/electrolyte balance and tissue perfusion.

questions.question: A patient who speaks limited English is consenting for surgery. To individualize care appropriately, the nurse should:
choices: Proceed because consent was signed earlier
Rely on gestures and pictures alone
Use a family child to interpret for speed
questions.explanation: A qualified medical interpreter ensures accurate communication and valid informed consent. Family members, especially minors, are not appropriate substitutes for clinical interpretation.

questions.question: A patient's understanding of the surgical procedure and informed consent is addressed in which PNDS domain?
questions.explanation: Knowledge, rights, consent, and anxiety are components of the Behavioral Responses domain (D3) in the PNDS model.

questions.question: When developing the plan for a patient with poorly controlled diabetes, which individualized intervention is most important perioperatively?
choices: Assuming normal healing with no special measures
Establishing a perioperative glucose monitoring and management protocol
Withholding all glucose monitoring until recovery
questions.explanation: Diabetic patients require perioperative glucose monitoring and management to reduce infection and impaired wound healing. This comorbidity-specific intervention individualizes the plan.

questions.question: Documentation and coordination of care are encompassed in which PNDS domain?
questions.explanation: The Health System domain (D4) addresses documentation, care coordination, and the structures and processes supporting perioperative care.

questions.question: A morbidly obese patient is scheduled for abdominal surgery. Which individualized consideration should be incorporated into positioning and equipment planning?
choices: Appropriately rated table, equipment, and additional padding for pressure points
Standard-weight table and routine padding only
questions.explanation: Obesity requires bariatric-rated equipment and enhanced padding to prevent pressure injury and ensure safe positioning. These adaptations individualize the plan to the patient's body habitus.

questions.question: According to AORN, which area of a sterile gown is considered sterile?
choices: From chest level to the level of the sterile field and the sleeves from 2 inches above the elbow to the cuff
Only the cuffs of the sleeves
From the neckline to the waist on all sides
The entire gown front and back
questions.explanation: A sterile gown is considered sterile in front from chest level to the level of the sterile field and at the sleeves from 2 inches above the elbow to the cuff.

questions.question: A patient is placed in the lithotomy position for a vaginal hysterectomy. Which nerve is at greatest risk of injury from improper positioning of the legs in the stirrups?
questions.explanation: In lithotomy, compression of the lateral aspect of the knee against the stirrup can injure the common peroneal nerve, causing foot drop.

questions.question: According to AORN guidelines, when should the initial (baseline) surgical count be performed?
choices: Before the procedure begins, to establish a baseline
Only at the end of the procedure
questions.explanation: The initial count establishes a baseline and must be completed before the procedure begins so all subsequent counts have a starting reference.

questions.question: In a monopolar electrosurgical circuit, what is the primary function of the dispersive (return) electrode?
choices: To concentrate current at the surgical site
To safely collect current and return it to the generator over a large surface area
To insulate the patient from radiofrequency energy
To activate the generator's foot pedal
questions.explanation: The dispersive electrode disperses the current over a large surface area so it returns to the generator without producing enough heat to burn the patient.

questions.question: Which step of the nursing process is the circulating RN prohibited from delegating to unlicensed assistive personnel?
choices: Nursing assessment, diagnosis, planning, and evaluation
Transporting the patient to the OR
Counting sponges with the scrub person
questions.explanation: Assessment, nursing diagnosis, outcome identification, planning, and evaluation are non-delegable professional nursing judgments reserved for the RN; only certain interventions may be delegated.

questions.question: When passing a scalpel to the surgeon, the scrub person should use which method to reduce the risk of sharps injury?
choices: Pass it blade-first toward the surgeon
Hand it directly into the surgeon's open palm
Toss it gently onto the Mayo stand
Use a hands-free or neutral zone technique
questions.explanation: AORN recommends a hands-free (neutral zone) technique for passing sharps so two people never touch the device simultaneously, reducing percutaneous injuries.

questions.question: A sterile drape that extends below the level of the table edge is considered:
choices: Sterile only at and above table level; the portion below the table edge is not sterile
Contaminated entirely and must be replaced
Sterile if it was draped by a scrubbed person
questions.explanation: Only the part of a draped table at table level and above is considered sterile; any portion extending below the table edge is not sterile and must not be brought back up.

questions.question: When positioning a patient in the supine position, the arms are placed on armboards abducted to no more than what angle to protect the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: Arms on armboards should be abducted less than 90 degrees to prevent stretch injury to the brachial plexus.

questions.question: Who should perform surgical counts according to AORN recommendations?
choices: The surgeon and the scrub person without the RN
Two persons, one of whom is the RN circulator, counting concurrently
Any single member of the surgical team
questions.explanation: Counts are performed by two individuals, typically the scrub person and the RN circulator, who count concurrently and audibly to provide a verification safeguard.

questions.question: A circulating nurse is preparing to place a dispersive electrode pad on a patient. Which site is most appropriate?
choices: Over scar tissue from a prior surgery
Over a bony prominence such as the scapula
On a clean, dry, well-vascularized muscle mass close to the surgical site
Over a metal implant such as a hip prosthesis
questions.explanation: AORN recommends placing the return electrode on clean, dry skin over a well-vascularized muscle mass as close as practical to the operative site, avoiding bony prominences, scar tissue, and implants.

questions.question: The primary patient-safety responsibility of the circulating RN during an operative procedure is to:
choices: Coordinate care and continuously assess the patient and environment
Maintain the sterile field by gowning team members
questions.explanation: The circulating RN manages the overall care of the patient, monitors the environment and patient status, and coordinates the activities of the perioperative team.

questions.question: A wound created during a clean elective procedure that does not enter the respiratory, alimentary, genital, or urinary tracts is classified as:
questions.explanation: A Class I clean wound is an uninfected operative wound with no inflammation and no entry into a colonized tract.

questions.question: The neckline, shoulders, and back of a sterile gown are considered:
choices: Sterile until the gown becomes damp
Sterile only when the gown is wraparound style
Sterile because they were packaged sterile
Not sterile because they cannot be continuously observed
questions.explanation: Areas that cannot be continuously monitored, such as the neckline, shoulders, axillary region, and back of the gown, are considered not sterile.

questions.question: Which method of hair removal is recommended by AORN to minimize the risk of surgical site infection?
questions.explanation: AORN recommends clipping with electric clippers rather than shaving with razors, which create microabrasions that increase infection risk.

questions.question: During a sponge count, the two team members should count in which manner?
choices: Audibly and concurrently while viewing the items
One counts and the other records without watching
questions.explanation: Concurrent, audible counting while both persons visualize each item ensures accuracy and shared accountability.

questions.question: What distinguishes bipolar electrosurgery from monopolar electrosurgery?
choices: Bipolar cannot be used for coagulation
In bipolar, current flows between the two tips of the instrument and a return pad is not needed
Bipolar requires a dispersive electrode pad
Bipolar uses higher voltage than monopolar
questions.explanation: In bipolar electrosurgery the active and return functions are both performed at the instrument tips, so current passes only through the tissue between them and no patient return electrode is required.

questions.question: A scrub person notices the surgeon is about to use an implant whose lot number was not recorded. The best action is to:
choices: Allow the implant since the surgeon is in charge
Record the number from memory after the case
Ask the circulator to estimate the number
Stop and ensure the lot/serial number is documented before implantation
questions.explanation: Implant lot and serial numbers must be captured before or at the time of use to support traceability and patient safety recalls; documentation cannot be reconstructed from memory.

questions.question: Absorbable suture is best described as suture that:
choices: Is digested or hydrolyzed by the body over time
Must always be removed by a clinician
Is made only of stainless steel
questions.explanation: Absorbable sutures lose tensile strength and are broken down by enzymatic digestion or hydrolysis, so they do not require removal.

questions.question: When a sterile item is found to be wet from strike-through, the BEST action is to:
choices: Consider it contaminated and remove it from the sterile field
Use it only if the package is otherwise intact
Dry it with a sterile towel and use it
Cover the wet area with a sterile drape
questions.explanation: Moisture provides a pathway for microorganisms to travel from a nonsterile to a sterile surface (strike-through), so the item is contaminated and must be removed.

questions.question: A patient in the prone position requires chest rolls. The primary purpose of chest rolls placed from the clavicle to the iliac crest is to:
choices: Increase venous return to the heart
Elevate the head above the heart
Allow chest expansion and reduce abdominal pressure
questions.explanation: Chest rolls support the thorax, allowing the abdomen to hang freely so the diaphragm can move and venous return is not impeded by abdominal compression.

questions.question: At minimum, surgical counts should be performed at which points during a procedure?
choices: Before the procedure, before closure of a cavity, before wound closure, and at skin closure or relief of personnel
Only at the beginning and end
questions.explanation: AORN recommends counts before the procedure (baseline), before closure of a cavity or organ, before wound closure, at skin closure, and at any permanent relief of the scrub or circulating personnel.

questions.question: Return electrode monitoring (REM) technology primarily protects the patient by doing what?
choices: Monitoring impedance of the dual-foil pad and deactivating the generator if contact is inadequate
questions.explanation: REM uses a split (dual-foil) pad to continuously monitor impedance at the pad-skin interface and stops energy delivery if contact quality drops, preventing return-electrode burns.

questions.question: Which activity is within the scope of practice of the RN first assistant (RNFA)?
choices: Providing hemostasis, suturing, and tissue handling under surgeon direction
questions.explanation: The RNFA performs intraoperative technical assisting tasks such as hemostasis, suturing, and tissue handling under the direction of the surgeon, but does not perform the surgeon's role.

questions.question: During cell salvage (autotransfusion), blood collected from the surgical field is processed primarily to:
choices: Separate plasma for the blood bank
Wash and concentrate red blood cells for reinfusion
questions.explanation: Cell salvage systems aspirate, wash, and concentrate the patient's own red cells so they can be reinfused, reducing the need for allogeneic transfusion.

questions.question: During surgical hand antisepsis using an alcohol-based hand rub product, before the first application of the day the nurse should:
choices: Scrub with a brush for 5 minutes
Prewash hands and forearms with soap and water and dry completely
Don sterile gloves before applying the rub
Apply the product to dry hands without any preparation
questions.explanation: Before the first alcohol-based surgical hand rub of the day, hands and forearms should be washed with soap and water and dried completely, and washed again any time they become visibly soiled.

questions.question: Why should alcohol-based skin prep agents be allowed to fully dry before draping and the use of electrosurgery?
choices: To prevent a surgical fire from ignitable vapors
To allow the iodine to oxidize
questions.explanation: Alcohol-based preps are flammable; pooled solution and vapors can ignite, so the prep must be completely dry before draping and energy use.

questions.question: When permanent relief of either the scrub person or circulating nurse occurs, what count action is required?
choices: The count is deferred to the end of the case
A complete count of all items must be performed
questions.explanation: A full count of sponges, sharps, and instruments is performed whenever permanent relief of scrub or circulating personnel occurs to maintain accountability.

questions.question: A patient with a permanent pacemaker is scheduled for surgery requiring electrosurgery. Which action best reduces the risk of electromagnetic interference?
choices: Avoid all forms of electrosurgery entirely without consultation
Place the dispersive pad directly over the pacemaker generator
Use monopolar mode at maximum power
Use bipolar electrosurgery when possible and keep the current path away from the device
questions.explanation: Bipolar electrosurgery limits current to the instrument tips, reducing electromagnetic interference; the current path between active and dispersive electrodes should be kept away from the cardiac device.

questions.question: Par level in OR supply management refers to:
choices: The maximum a vendor will ship per order
The cost of an item including markup
The expiration interval of a sterile item
The minimum stock quantity that triggers reorder to avoid stockouts
questions.explanation: A par level is the predetermined minimum on-hand quantity at which an item is reordered to ensure availability without overstocking.

questions.question: Which hemostatic agent works by providing a physical matrix that promotes platelet aggregation and is absorbable?
questions.explanation: Absorbable gelatin sponge (e.g., Gelfoam) provides a scaffold that supports clot formation and is absorbed by the body.

questions.question: Which technique allows a scrubbed person to don their own gloves without their bare hands touching the outside of the glove?
questions.explanation: In closed gloving, the hands remain inside the gown sleeves and never extend past the cuff, so bare skin never contacts the outer glove surface.

questions.question: Trendelenburg position increases the risk of which physiologic effect?
choices: Increased venous return and elevated intracranial pressure
questions.explanation: Head-down tilt shifts blood and abdominal contents cephalad, raising venous return, intracranial, and intraocular pressures while reducing pulmonary compliance.

questions.question: What is the recommended action when a count discrepancy cannot be resolved?
choices: Wait until the patient is in recovery to investigate
Notify the surgeon, perform a methodical search, and obtain an intraoperative radiograph if the item is not found
questions.explanation: The surgeon is notified, the team searches the field, drapes, floor, and trash, and an intraoperative radiograph is obtained when the item remains unaccounted for.

questions.question: Which mechanism explains a capacitive coupling burn during laparoscopic monopolar electrosurgery?
choices: Excessive smoke accumulation in the abdomen
Direct contact of the active electrode with bowel
Failure of the return electrode pad adhesive
Current induced through intact insulation into an adjacent conductor such as a metal cannula
questions.explanation: Capacitive coupling occurs when current passes through intact insulation to a nearby conductor (for example a metal cannula or trocar), which can then discharge into tissue and cause an unintended burn.

questions.question: FIFO inventory rotation in the OR storeroom means:
choices: Items are restocked only on Fridays
Most expensive items are issued first
Heaviest items are placed in front
Items with the earliest expiration dates are used first
questions.explanation: First-In, First-Out rotation places older or sooner-to-expire stock in front so it is used before newer stock, reducing waste from expiration.

questions.question: A surgical implant such as an orthopedic plate must be documented in the patient record with:
questions.explanation: Implant documentation must include manufacturer, lot or serial number, type, and size to support traceability and recall management.

questions.question: The 1-inch margin at the edge of an opened sterile wrapper is considered:
choices: Sterile if the package was not damp
questions.explanation: A 1-inch (2.5 cm) margin at the edge of an opened sterile wrapper is considered not sterile.

questions.question: Which patient factor is the most significant intrinsic risk for developing a pressure injury during a long surgical procedure?
choices: High body mass with good nutrition
questions.explanation: Diabetes and impaired perfusion reduce tissue tolerance to pressure, markedly increasing the risk of intraoperative pressure injury.

questions.question: A retained surgical item (RSI) is most commonly which type of object?
choices: A soft good such as a sponge or gauze
questions.explanation: Soft goods, particularly surgical sponges, are the most frequently retained surgical items.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce the risk of insulation failure injuries during laparoscopic electrosurgery?
choices: Coil the active electrode cord tightly around a metal clamp
Activate the electrode only when in contact with target tissue and inspect insulation before use
questions.explanation: Inspecting insulation for breaks before use and activating only when the active tip is in clear view and in contact with target tissue minimizes stray-current and insulation-failure injuries.

questions.question: Consignment inventory in surgical services is best described as:
choices: Expired stock returned to the manufacturer
Vendor-owned stock kept on site and paid for only when used
questions.explanation: Consigned inventory remains the property of the vendor and is paid for only when consumed, which is common for high-cost, low-volume implants.

questions.question: The circulating nurse notices the surgeon's gown sleeve has become wet at the field. The most appropriate action is to:
choices: Ignore it because the gown is still on
Apply tape over the wet area
Recognize strike-through contamination and assist with a gown change
Wait until the case ends to address it
questions.explanation: Moisture strike-through compromises the sterile barrier, so the affected gown is considered contaminated and should be changed.

questions.question: When opening a sterile wrapped package held in the hand, the circulator should open the flap:
choices: Away from themselves first, then the sides, then toward themselves last
questions.explanation: The first flap is opened away from the body to avoid reaching over the sterile contents, followed by the side flaps and finally the flap nearest the body.

questions.question: During a procedure in the lateral position, an axillary roll (chest roll) is placed to:
choices: Relieve pressure on the dependent brachial plexus and axillary vessels
questions.explanation: The axillary roll is positioned caudal to the dependent axilla to lift the thorax and prevent compression of the brachial plexus and axillary neurovascular structures.

questions.question: Which technology uses radiofrequency tags embedded in sponges to detect retained items?
questions.explanation: RF detection systems use a handheld or mat-based wand to identify sponges containing embedded radiofrequency tags, serving as an adjunct to manual counting.

questions.question: Why should the surgeon avoid activating the electrosurgical unit in the open-circuit (non-contact) state at high voltage near other instruments?
choices: It can cause direct coupling, transferring current to nearby conductive instruments
It is required for proper grounding
questions.explanation: Activating the active electrode while it is touching or near another conductive instrument can cause direct coupling, transferring current to that instrument and burning tissue in contact with it.

questions.question: Which item must be discarded in a red biohazard (regulated medical waste) bag?
choices: A used disposable patient gown without visible soiling
A sponge saturated and dripping with blood
questions.explanation: Items saturated or dripping with blood or other potentially infectious material are regulated medical waste and must be red-bagged; clean or lightly soiled items go in regular trash.

questions.question: Bone wax is used during surgery primarily to:
choices: Control bleeding from cut bone surfaces
questions.explanation: Bone wax provides a mechanical (tamponade) barrier that controls oozing from cancellous bone surfaces.

questions.question: A scrubbed team member should keep their hands and arms:
choices: Above waist level and within the sterile field, in view at all times
Tucked under the arms to conserve sterility
Below waist level when not in use
questions.explanation: Hands and arms must remain above waist level and within the boundaries of the sterile field where they can be continuously monitored.

questions.question: When prepping with chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG), which site is contraindicated for its use?
questions.explanation: CHG can cause keratitis if it contacts the eye and ototoxicity if it enters the middle ear, so its use is contraindicated at these sites.

questions.question: Adjunct technologies such as bar-coding and RF detection are intended to do what relative to manual counting?
choices: Eliminate the need for a circulating nurse
Supplement, not replace, manual counting procedures
Be used only when counts are incorrect
questions.explanation: AORN positions these technologies as adjuncts that supplement standardized manual counting; they do not replace it.

questions.question: Which element must always be documented on the intraoperative nursing record regarding surgical counts?
choices: The results of initial, closing, and final counts and any actions taken for a discrepancy
The surgeon's verbal agreement that counts are unnecessary
Counts only for cases involving open cavities
Only the final count if it is correct
questions.explanation: The intraoperative record must reflect the results of all counts performed and any corrective actions taken if a discrepancy occurs, providing a complete account of count reconciliation.

questions.question: During which phase of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist does the team confirm patient identity, surgical site, and procedure before the patient receives anesthesia?
questions.explanation: The sign-in phase occurs before induction of anesthesia and confirms patient identity, site, procedure, and consent.

questions.question: When documenting an implant in the intraoperative record, which information is essential to capture?
choices: The retail cost of the implant
Only the body site of implantation
The manufacturer, lot or serial number, type, and size of the implant
questions.explanation: Implant documentation must include identifying data such as manufacturer, lot/serial number, type, and size to support recalls and traceability.

questions.question: The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist time-out is performed at which point in the procedure?
choices: Before the patient enters the room
After the patient leaves the room
questions.explanation: The time-out is conducted immediately before skin incision, with all team members participating to confirm correct patient, site, and procedure.

questions.question: A specimen is sent to pathology. Which detail is most important to document on the intraoperative record?
choices: The number of staff in the room
The type of specimen, its source/site, and any special handling instructions
The temperature of the operating room
The brand of the specimen container
questions.explanation: Specimen documentation should identify the specimen type, anatomical source, laterality if applicable, and any special handling such as fresh or frozen to ensure correct processing.

questions.question: Which WHO Surgical Safety Checklist phase occurs before the patient leaves the operating room?
questions.explanation: The sign-out phase takes place before the patient leaves the OR and includes confirmation of the procedure, counts, and specimen labeling.

questions.question: Which positioning detail should be recorded in the intraoperative nursing record?
choices: Only the height of the operating table
The position used, positioning devices, and the condition of the skin before and after the procedure
Only that the patient was 'positioned properly'
questions.explanation: Documentation must specify the patient position, devices used to maintain it, and pre- and postoperative skin assessment to demonstrate that protective measures were taken.

questions.question: The Joint Commission Universal Protocol was developed primarily to prevent which adverse event?
questions.explanation: The Universal Protocol targets the prevention of wrong-site, wrong-procedure, and wrong-person surgery through verification, marking, and a time-out.

questions.question: What is the correct method for correcting a written error in the paper intraoperative record?
choices: Draw a single line through the error, initial, and date it, leaving it legible
Use correction fluid to cover the error
Tear out the page and rewrite it
questions.explanation: A single line through the error keeps the original entry legible and, with initials and date, preserves the integrity of the legal record.

questions.question: Which of the following are the three principal components of The Joint Commission Universal Protocol?
choices: Preoperative verification, site marking, and time-out
questions.explanation: The Universal Protocol consists of a preoperative verification process, marking the procedure site, and performing a time-out before the procedure begins.

questions.question: The intraoperative record is best described in legal terms as:
choices: A record owned solely by the surgeon
An informal communication tool with no legal standing
A legal document that can be used as evidence in litigation
A document that may be discarded after discharge
questions.explanation: The perioperative nursing record is a legal document and can be entered as evidence; accurate, complete, and timely entries are essential.

questions.question: When marking a surgical site under the Universal Protocol, the mark should be made so that it is:
choices: Placed only by the circulating nurse
Visible after the patient is prepped and draped
Located at least 10 cm from the incision
Removed before the patient enters the OR
questions.explanation: The site mark must be unambiguous and remain visible after skin preparation and draping so it can be confirmed during the time-out.

questions.question: Which component of SBAR conveys the patient's current vital signs and clinical status?
questions.explanation: In SBAR, Assessment communicates the nurse's evaluation of the patient's current condition, including vital signs and clinical findings.

questions.question: Who should ideally mark the surgical site according to the Universal Protocol?
choices: The licensed practitioner who will perform the procedure
questions.explanation: Site marking should be done by the licensed independent practitioner who is ultimately accountable for and present during the procedure.

questions.question: During hand-off to the PACU nurse, the receiving nurse repeats back the information given. This practice is called:
questions.explanation: Read-back is a verification technique in which the receiver restates the communicated information to confirm accuracy and shared understanding.

questions.question: During the surgical time-out, which team member typically initiates and leads the process?
choices: A designated team member, often the circulating nurse
questions.explanation: A designated member, frequently the circulating nurse, initiates the time-out, but all members must actively participate.

questions.question: According to the Spaulding classification, which category of medical device requires sterilization?
choices: Environmental surfaces such as bed rails
Semicritical items that contact mucous membranes
Noncritical items that contact intact skin
Critical items that enter sterile tissue or the vascular system
questions.explanation: Spaulding classifies items entering sterile tissue or the vascular system as critical, mandating sterilization because any microbial contamination poses a high infection risk.

questions.question: Immediately after a surgical procedure, when should the initial treatment of contaminated instruments begin to prevent organic debris from drying?
choices: Only after instruments reach the decontamination room
After the terminal cleaning of the OR suite
At the start of the next business day
At the point of use during and immediately after the procedure
questions.explanation: Point-of-use treatment, such as keeping instruments moist and removing gross soil during and right after the procedure, prevents bioburden from drying and hardening so later cleaning is more effective.

questions.question: A flexible gastrointestinal endoscope that contacts intact mucous membranes is classified under Spaulding as which type of device?
choices: Semicritical, requiring at least high-level disinfection
questions.explanation: Devices contacting mucous membranes or nonintact skin are semicritical and require at minimum high-level disinfection.

questions.question: A biological indicator (BI) provides which level of sterilization process monitoring?
choices: It confirms the package reached the storage area intact
It directly demonstrates that the process killed resistant spores
It measures the pH of the sterilant solution
It only verifies that steam contacted the package surface
questions.explanation: A BI contains live, highly resistant bacterial spores, so a negative result directly demonstrates that the sterilization process was lethal to microorganisms.

questions.question: A scrub person notices that a surgical clamp's jaws no longer align and the ratchet does not hold. What is the most appropriate action?
choices: Remove it from service and tag it for repair or replacement
Apply extra lubricant to the box lock and reuse it
Sterilize it again to restore its function
Continue using it if it still closes partway
questions.explanation: Instruments with misaligned jaws or non-holding ratchets are defective and must be removed from service and tagged for repair, because they can compromise tissue handling and patient safety.

questions.question: Which item is correctly categorized as noncritical under the Spaulding classification?
choices: A blood pressure cuff that contacts intact skin
questions.explanation: Noncritical items contact only intact skin, which is an effective barrier, so they require low- or intermediate-level disinfection rather than sterilization.

questions.question: The Bowie-Dick test is performed to evaluate which aspect of a dynamic-air-removal (prevacuum) steam sterilizer?
choices: Adequate air removal and steam penetration
questions.explanation: The Bowie-Dick test detects air leaks and inadequate air removal that would prevent rapid, uniform steam penetration in a prevacuum sterilizer.

questions.question: Which solution is appropriate to keep instruments moist during transport to decontamination?
choices: Sterile water or a manufacturer-approved enzymatic pretreatment product
questions.explanation: Saline is corrosive and can pit instruments, so water or a manufacturer-recommended enzymatic spray or gel is preferred to keep soil from drying without damaging instruments.

questions.question: The Spaulding classification assigns the level of reprocessing primarily based on what factor?
choices: The material composition of the device
The degree of infection risk associated with how the device contacts the patient
questions.explanation: Spaulding stratifies devices by the infection risk posed by how the item contacts the patient, dictating critical, semicritical, or noncritical reprocessing.

questions.question: How often should the Bowie-Dick test be run in a dynamic-air-removal steam sterilizer?
choices: Each day the sterilizer is used, in the first cycle
questions.explanation: ANSI/AAMI ST79 specifies running a Bowie-Dick test each day the prevacuum sterilizer is used, typically in the first cycle after the warm-up cycle.

questions.question: During inspection, an instrument with a lumen is being evaluated. Which step best verifies the lumen is clear of debris?
choices: Weighing the instrument before and after cleaning
Visual inspection of the exterior surface only
Holding it up to room light and assuming patency
Flushing the lumen and using magnification or a borescope to verify cleanliness
questions.explanation: Lumened instruments require flushing plus magnification or verification tools because internal channels cannot be assessed by external visual inspection alone.

questions.question: Why is point-of-use treatment performed on contaminated instruments immediately after a procedure?
choices: To replace the need for manual cleaning entirely
To sterilize the instruments at the bedside
To lubricate hinged instruments before storage
To keep soil moist and prevent it from drying and hardening on the device
questions.explanation: Point-of-use treatment keeps gross soil and bioburden moist so debris does not dry onto instruments, which would make later cleaning far more difficult.

questions.question: The Bowie-Dick test cycle should be run in an empty chamber except for the test pack and preceded by what?
questions.explanation: A warm-up cycle is run first to bring the sterilizer to operating temperature so the Bowie-Dick test accurately evaluates air removal.

questions.question: Why are box locks and serrated jaws of instruments opened during the cleaning process?
choices: To prevent the instrument from rusting
To expose all surfaces and crevices to the cleaning agent and sterilant
To reduce the weight of the instrument set
To make the set easier to count
questions.explanation: Opening box locks and articulations exposes hidden crevices to cleaning solution and sterilant, ensuring soil removal and sterilant contact on all surfaces.

questions.question: Which solution is appropriate for point-of-use treatment to keep instruments moist before transport to decontamination?
choices: A saline soak in a basin
An enzymatic or instrument-safe pretreatment product per manufacturer instructions
Sterile water heated to 80 degrees Celsius
questions.explanation: Manufacturer-validated enzymatic or transport gels and sprays are used at point of use; saline is corrosive and should be avoided on instruments.

questions.question: A Class 5 chemical indicator is best described as which of the following?
choices: A process indicator that only shows exposure to the process
An integrating indicator that reacts to all critical parameters of the cycle
An emulating indicator equivalent to a biological indicator
A single-variable indicator for temperature only
questions.explanation: Class 5 integrating indicators react to all critical process variables (time, temperature, and steam quality) over a stated range, correlating to the performance of a BI.

questions.question: The decontamination area of a sterile processing department should be maintained under which air pressure relationship?
choices: Equal pressure with no directional airflow
Positive pressure relative to adjacent areas
Negative pressure relative to adjacent areas
questions.explanation: The decontamination area is kept under negative pressure so contaminated air flows into the room rather than out, preventing spread of contaminants to clean areas.

questions.question: Why should saline not be used to soak or rinse surgical instruments during point-of-use treatment?
choices: It is corrosive and can cause pitting and rusting of instruments
It is too expensive for routine use
questions.explanation: Saline is corrosive to stainless steel and can cause pitting, staining, and rusting, so it is not used on instruments.

questions.question: Which class of chemical indicator is a process indicator used to distinguish processed from unprocessed items?
questions.explanation: Class 1 (process) indicators, such as autoclave tape, show that an item has been exposed to a sterilization process and help prevent mix-ups.

questions.question: In a sterile processing department, the workflow is designed to move instruments in which direction?
choices: Randomly, as long as items are sterilized eventually
From clean to dirty to allow recontamination checks
In both directions to maximize efficiency
One-way from decontamination to clean assembly to sterile storage
questions.explanation: A unidirectional flow from dirty to clean to sterile prevents cross-contamination by ensuring contaminated and clean items never share the same path.

questions.question: What is the primary action of an enzymatic detergent used in instrument cleaning?
choices: It breaks down organic soil such as blood, protein, and lipids
It raises the pH to dissolve metal oxides
questions.explanation: Enzymatic detergents contain enzymes such as proteases and lipases that break down organic bioburden, making it easier to remove during cleaning.

questions.question: An internal chemical indicator should be placed in which location within each package?
choices: Taped to the sterilizer chamber wall
Outside the package next to the lot label
In the area considered most difficult for the sterilant to reach
questions.explanation: An internal CI is placed in the location within the package judged least accessible to the sterilant so that a pass indicates penetration throughout the package.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an enzymatic detergent used in instrument decontamination?
choices: To break down and loosen organic soil such as blood and protein
To passivate the stainless steel surface
questions.explanation: Enzymatic detergents contain enzymes that digest organic material like blood, fat, and protein, loosening bioburden so it can be rinsed away during cleaning.

questions.question: Cleaning must always precede disinfection or sterilization primarily because:
choices: Soil improves steam penetration into lumens
Organic and inorganic soil shields microorganisms from the sterilant
Cleaning replaces the need for a biological indicator
questions.explanation: Residual soil can shield microorganisms and prevent the sterilant from contacting all surfaces, so thorough cleaning is essential before any sterilization or disinfection.

questions.question: Which class of agents is a recognized trigger for malignant hyperthermia (MH)?
questions.explanation: Volatile inhalational anesthetics such as sevoflurane, desflurane, and isoflurane are classic MH triggers; opioids, benzodiazepines, and propofol are nontriggering.

questions.question: A surgical patient suddenly loses 1,500 mL of blood. Which set of vital sign changes is most consistent with Class III hemorrhagic shock?
choices: Mild tachycardia with normal blood pressure
Marked tachycardia, hypotension, and decreased urine output
Normal heart rate and blood pressure
questions.explanation: Class III hemorrhage (roughly 30-40 percent volume loss) produces significant tachycardia, falling blood pressure, and oliguria. These findings signal the need for aggressive resuscitation.

questions.question: Which neuromuscular blocking agent is a known trigger for malignant hyperthermia?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, is the only paralytic that triggers MH; nondepolarizing agents are safe.

questions.question: The three components of the lethal triad that worsen outcomes in massive hemorrhage are:
questions.explanation: The lethal triad consists of coagulopathy, metabolic acidosis, and hypothermia, which reinforce one another and increase mortality. Interrupting any one element improves survival.

questions.question: What is the earliest and most sensitive sign of malignant hyperthermia during general anesthesia?
choices: Rising end-tidal CO2 unresponsive to increased ventilation
A sudden temperature spike to 40 C
questions.explanation: An unexplained, rapidly rising end-tidal CO2 that does not respond to increased minute ventilation is the earliest sensitive sign of MH.

questions.question: A balanced massive transfusion protocol delivers blood products in approximately what ratio?
choices: 3:1:1 of red cells, plasma, and platelets
1:1:1 of plasma, platelets, and packed red blood cells
1:2:4 of platelets, plasma, and red cells
questions.explanation: A balanced 1:1:1 ratio of plasma, platelets, and packed red blood cells most closely reconstitutes whole blood and limits dilutional coagulopathy. This approach is the standard for massive transfusion.

questions.question: Hyperthermia in malignant hyperthermia is best characterized as which type of sign?
choices: A late sign of the crisis
questions.explanation: Despite the name, hyperthermia is a LATE sign of MH; metabolic signs such as rising end-tidal CO2 and tachycardia appear first.

questions.question: Why is maintaining normothermia a priority during massive transfusion?
choices: Hypothermia impairs the clotting cascade and platelet function
questions.explanation: Hypothermia slows enzymatic clotting reactions and impairs platelet aggregation, worsening hemorrhage. Keeping the patient warm helps preserve coagulation.

questions.question: What is the recommended initial intravenous dose of dantrolene for an acute MH crisis?
questions.explanation: The initial dantrolene dose is 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated as needed until signs of hypermetabolism resolve.

questions.question: During a code in the OR, the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. The most appropriate immediate intervention is:
questions.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a shockable rhythm treated with immediate unsynchronized defibrillation. Early defibrillation is the single most important determinant of survival in VF.

questions.question: Which drug treats malignant hyperthermia by inhibiting calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum?
questions.explanation: Dantrolene is the specific MH antidote; it blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, halting sustained contraction and hypermetabolism.

questions.question: Which of the following is a nonshockable cardiac arrest rhythm?
questions.explanation: Asystole and pulseless electrical activity are nonshockable; they are managed with CPR and epinephrine rather than defibrillation. Shocking asystole provides no benefit.

questions.question: Which finding is a hallmark muscular sign of MH after succinylcholine administration?
questions.explanation: Masseter (jaw) rigidity following succinylcholine can be an early warning of MH, sometimes progressing to generalized muscle rigidity.

questions.question: Before delivering a defibrillation shock in the OR, the circulating nurse should ensure that:
choices: All team members are clear and oxygen flow is managed away from the field
The oxygen source is left flowing for the patient
questions.explanation: Defibrillation near an oxygen-enriched field poses a fire risk, so flowing oxygen should be directed away or paused and everyone must be clear before the shock. This protects both patient and staff.

questions.question: During an MH crisis, after stopping triggering agents, the provider should ventilate the patient with:
questions.explanation: Hyperventilation with 100% oxygen at high fresh gas flows helps clear residual volatile agent and treat the hypermetabolic CO2 production.

questions.question: A patient refuses a recommended surgical procedure after being fully informed of the risks and benefits. Which ethical principle does the nurse uphold by supporting the patient's decision?
questions.explanation: Autonomy is the patient's right to self-determination, including the right to refuse treatment after being adequately informed.

questions.question: The ethical principle of beneficence requires the perioperative nurse to do which of the following?
choices: Act in the best interest of and promote good for the patient
Always tell the patient the truth
Avoid causing harm to the patient
questions.explanation: Beneficence is the duty to act for the benefit of others and to promote good for the patient.

questions.question: Nonmaleficence is best described by which statement?
choices: The obligation to do no harm
The obligation to respect a patient's choices
The obligation to allocate care equitably
questions.explanation: Nonmaleficence is the ethical duty to avoid causing harm to the patient -- captured in the phrase 'first, do no harm.'

questions.question: A nurse ensures that two patients with the same condition receive equivalent standards of care regardless of their insurance status. Which ethical principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Justice is the principle of fairness and equitable distribution of care and resources among patients.

questions.question: The ethical principle of fidelity most directly obligates the nurse to do what?
choices: Keep commitments and remain faithful to professional responsibilities
Tell the truth in all communications
Respect the patient's right to refuse care
questions.explanation: Fidelity is the duty to keep promises, honor commitments, and remain loyal to one's professional obligations to the patient.

questions.question: When a nurse provides honest, complete information to a patient about an unexpected outcome, the nurse is practicing which ethical principle?
questions.explanation: Veracity is the duty to be truthful and not deceive patients, including honest disclosure of outcomes.

questions.question: Who is legally responsible for obtaining a patient's informed consent for a surgical procedure?
choices: The surgeon or physician performing the procedure
questions.explanation: Obtaining informed consent is the responsibility of the surgeon or physician performing the procedure, as they possess the knowledge of risks, benefits, and alternatives.

questions.question: What is the perioperative nurse's primary role regarding the informed consent document?
choices: Explaining the surgical risks and benefits to the patient
Determining whether the procedure is medically necessary
Deciding which alternatives the patient should consider
Verifying that consent was obtained and witnessing the signature
questions.explanation: The nurse verifies that informed consent has been obtained by the physician and witnesses the patient's signature; the nurse does not provide the disclosure of risks and alternatives.

questions.question: A patient scheduled for surgery says, 'I'm not really sure what they're going to do to me.' What is the nurse's most appropriate action?
choices: Reschedule the surgery for another day
Explain the procedure in detail to the patient
Have the patient sign the consent and proceed
Notify the surgeon so the consent process can be completed
questions.explanation: If the patient lacks understanding, informed consent is incomplete; the nurse must notify the surgeon, who is responsible for providing the disclosure.

questions.question: During PACU hand-off, the anesthesia provider should communicate all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Intraoperative fluids, blood loss, and urine output
Type of anesthesia and airway management
questions.explanation: A structured hand-off conveys clinically relevant data; the surgeon's schedule is irrelevant.

questions.question: A patient scheduled for surgery has received preoperative midazolam and now appears drowsy when asked to sign the consent. The most appropriate action is to:
choices: Have a family member sign on the patient's behalf
Ask the patient to sign quickly before more sedation takes effect
Notify the surgeon, as consent should be obtained before sedation
Proceed because the surgeon already explained the procedure
questions.explanation: Informed consent must be obtained before administering sedatives or opioids that impair the patient's ability to understand and decide; the surgeon should be notified.

questions.question: Which statement about assigning the ASA E modifier is correct?
choices: It replaces the numeric ASA class entirely
It is appended to any ASA class (I-V) when the procedure is an emergency
It is used only for trauma patients
It can only be applied to ASA IV and V patients
questions.explanation: The E modifier may be added to any ASA Physical Status class from I through V when the operation qualifies as an emergency.

questions.question: The most common cause of early airway obstruction in the recovering anesthetized patient is:
choices: The tongue falling against the posterior pharynx
questions.explanation: Relaxation of pharyngeal muscles allows the tongue to fall back against the posterior pharynx, the most frequent cause of obstruction.

questions.question: Standard adult NPO guidance from current anesthesia practice generally recommends no clear liquids for how long before elective surgery?
questions.explanation: Current ASA fasting guidelines allow clear liquids up to 2 hours before elective surgery requiring anesthesia.

questions.question: An otherwise healthy patient presents for emergency appendectomy for acute appendicitis. The most appropriate ASA classification is?
questions.explanation: A healthy patient (ASA I) undergoing an emergency procedure receives the E modifier, yielding ASA I E.

questions.question: A first-line maneuver to relieve airway obstruction caused by the tongue in a PACU patient is:
questions.explanation: A jaw thrust or chin lift repositions the tongue and opens the airway, the appropriate first response to soft-tissue obstruction.

questions.question: According to standard fasting guidance, a light meal such as toast and clear liquids should be withheld for at least how long before elective anesthesia?
questions.explanation: A light meal requires a minimum 6-hour fast, while fried or fatty foods may require 8 hours or more before elective surgery.

questions.question: Which of the following is a well-controlled chronic condition that would typically place a patient at ASA II rather than ASA III?
questions.explanation: Mild, well-controlled conditions such as controlled asthma or controlled hypertension fit ASA II, whereas severe limitations indicate ASA III or higher.

questions.question: A PACU patient develops a high-pitched crowing sound with respiratory effort shortly after extubation. This most likely indicates:
questions.explanation: A high-pitched crowing or stridorous sound after extubation is the classic presentation of laryngospasm.

questions.question: A patient reports allergies to bananas, avocados, and kiwi. The perioperative nurse should be most alert to the risk of:
questions.explanation: Allergies to bananas, avocados, kiwi, and chestnuts are associated with latex cross-reactivity, prompting latex-safe precautions.

questions.question: The ASA Physical Status classification includes clinical examples for adult, obstetric, and pediatric patients. The primary value of these examples is to?
choices: Improve consistency and reduce variability in classification
questions.explanation: ASA added clinical examples to improve interrater reliability and reduce variability in how clinicians assign physical status.

questions.question: Initial management of laryngospasm in the PACU includes:
choices: Positive-pressure ventilation with 100 percent oxygen and a jaw thrust
questions.explanation: Laryngospasm is first treated with positive-pressure ventilation, 100 percent oxygen, and a jaw thrust; persistent spasm may require succinylcholine.

questions.question: Which patient population is at highest risk for latex allergy?
choices: Patients with spina bifida or multiple prior surgeries
questions.explanation: Repeated mucosal exposure, as occurs with spina bifida and multiple surgeries, markedly increases the likelihood of latex sensitization.

questions.question: A pregnant patient at term with no complicating disease presents for a scheduled cesarean section. ASA guidance places normal uncomplicated pregnancy in which class?
questions.explanation: Normal pregnancy is considered ASA II under current ASA examples because it represents a mild physiologic alteration without substantive limitation.

questions.question: Which medication may be given for laryngospasm that does not break with positive-pressure ventilation?
questions.explanation: A small dose of succinylcholine relaxes the laryngeal muscles when positive-pressure ventilation alone fails to break the spasm.

questions.question: A patient takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Which laboratory value is most important to review before surgery?
questions.explanation: Warfarin's anticoagulant effect is monitored by the INR, which must be assessed and often normalized before surgery to reduce bleeding risk.

questions.question: Which patient is most appropriately classified as ASA IV?
choices: A patient with stable angina and good functional capacity
A patient with a 30 pack-year smoking history but normal function
A patient with ongoing sepsis and severe valve dysfunction
questions.explanation: ASA IV reflects severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life, such as ongoing sepsis or severe cardiac dysfunction.

questions.question: Residual neuromuscular blockade in the PACU is best identified by which finding?
choices: Sustained head lift greater than 5 seconds
Inability to sustain a head lift and weak grip
questions.explanation: Residual paralysis manifests as muscle weakness, including inability to sustain a 5-second head lift, weak grip, and impaired swallowing.

questions.question: A patient discloses taking ginkgo biloba, garlic, and fish oil supplements. The primary perioperative concern with these agents is:
questions.explanation: Ginkgo, garlic, and fish oil have antiplatelet or anticoagulant properties that increase perioperative bleeding risk and are often stopped before surgery.

questions.question: A surgical wound made under sterile conditions without entry into the respiratory, alimentary, genital, or uninfected urinary tract is classified as?
questions.explanation: Class I (Clean) wounds are uninfected operative wounds with no inflammation and no entry into the respiratory, GI, genital, or uninfected urinary tracts.

questions.question: A patient who received a nondepolarizing blocker shows residual weakness in the PACU. The appropriate reversal is:
questions.explanation: Residual nondepolarizing blockade is reversed with an anticholinesterase plus an antimuscarinic, or with sugammadex for rocuronium or vecuronium.

questions.question: Which herbal supplement is most associated with prolonged sedation and potentiation of anesthetic agents?
questions.explanation: Valerian acts on GABA pathways and can prolong the effects of anesthetics and sedatives, similar to its sedative-hypnotic action.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the difference between an expected outcome and a nursing intervention?
choices: An outcome is the action the nurse performs; an intervention is the result
An outcome is a measurable patient state to achieve; an intervention is the action taken to reach it
Both describe nurse actions in different terms
An outcome applies only to the postoperative phase
questions.explanation: An expected outcome describes the desired, measurable patient result, while an intervention is the nursing action performed to achieve that outcome.

questions.question: A patient on chronic warfarin therapy presents for an elective procedure. The individualized plan should prioritize:
choices: Ignoring the INR if surgery is minor
Coordinating anticoagulation management and assessing bleeding risk
questions.explanation: Anticoagulated patients need coordinated management of their therapy and bleeding-risk assessment. This individualizes the plan to prevent hemorrhagic complications.

questions.question: The acronym SMART, used in writing expected outcomes, indicates that outcomes should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and:
questions.explanation: SMART outcomes are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound, ensuring clear and evaluable goals.

questions.question: A patient reports a latex allergy during the preoperative interview. The most appropriate individualized action is to:
choices: Use latex products but monitor closely
Implement a latex-safe environment and verify supplies
Schedule the case last regardless of supplies
Document the allergy without changing supplies
questions.explanation: A latex allergy requires a latex-safe environment with verified non-latex supplies to prevent anaphylaxis. This is a critical individualized safety intervention.

questions.question: During which phase of the nursing process does the perioperative nurse collect data about the patient's allergies, medications, and surgical history?
questions.explanation: Data collection on allergies, medications, and history occurs during the assessment phase, forming the basis for the plan of care.

questions.question: When planning care for a patient who is deaf and uses sign language, the nurse should:
choices: Speak louder and slower to compensate
Assume the patient can read lips through the mask
Limit communication to written notes during anesthesia
Arrange for a qualified sign-language interpreter or agreed communication method
questions.explanation: A qualified interpreter or pre-agreed communication method ensures the deaf patient can participate in care. This individualizes the plan to a sensory disability.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correctly written, measurable expected outcome?
choices: The nurse will apply a forced-air warming blanket
The patient will be kept comfortable
The patient maintains a core temperature greater than 36 degrees C throughout the procedure
questions.explanation: A measurable outcome specifies an observable, quantifiable patient state, such as maintaining a core temperature above 36 degrees C; the others are interventions or vague goals.

questions.question: A 78-year-old patient takes multiple medications and has mild renal impairment. Which individualized concern is most relevant to the intraoperative plan?
choices: No need to review the medication list
Faster drug clearance than younger adults
Altered drug metabolism and clearance requiring careful agent selection
questions.explanation: Geriatric patients with renal impairment have altered drug metabolism and clearance, requiring careful agent and dose selection. This individualizes anesthetic and medication planning.

questions.question: A nurse writes: 'The patient demonstrates knowledge of postoperative wound care before discharge.' This outcome belongs to which PNDS domain?
questions.explanation: Demonstration of knowledge is a Behavioral Responses (D3) outcome, which encompasses patient learning and understanding.

questions.question: Using Maslow's hierarchy to prioritize, which intraoperative need takes precedence?
choices: Maintaining a patent airway and adequate oxygenation
questions.explanation: Physiologic needs such as airway and oxygenation are at the base of Maslow's hierarchy and take priority. Life-sustaining needs are addressed before higher-level needs.

questions.question: Maintenance of fluid and electrolyte balance during a lengthy procedure is an outcome within which PNDS domain?
questions.explanation: Fluid and electrolyte balance is a Physiologic Responses (D2) outcome, alongside thermoregulation and tissue perfusion.

questions.question: During a procedure the patient suddenly becomes hypotensive with no palpable pulse. Applying the ABC priority framework, the team should first:
choices: Address airway, breathing, and circulation immediately
questions.explanation: The ABC framework directs immediate attention to airway, breathing, and circulation in a life-threatening event. Physiologic stabilization precedes all other tasks.

questions.question: A patient has implanted jewelry that cannot be removed before electrosurgery. What is the rationale for the concern?
choices: Jewelry interferes with the laser only
There is no electrosurgical concern with jewelry
Jewelry blocks the surgical view only
Metal can become a path of concentrated current and cause a burn
questions.explanation: Conductive metal can provide an alternate, concentrated current path during monopolar electrosurgery, potentially causing a localized burn at the contact point.

questions.question: Routinely placing all OR waste in red bags is discouraged primarily because it:
choices: Greatly increases disposal cost without added safety
questions.explanation: Regulated medical waste disposal is far more expensive than regular waste, so over-segregating drives up cost without improving safety; only truly contaminated items belong in red bags.

questions.question: A ligature (tie) used to occlude a blood vessel without a needle is best described as:
choices: A free strand of suture material
questions.explanation: A ligature is a strand of suture material tied around a vessel or structure to achieve hemostasis without an attached needle.

questions.question: Which describes the correct sequence for surgical attire when scrubbing in?
choices: Gown first, then surgical hand antisepsis, then gloves
Surgical hand antisepsis, then gown, then gloves
Gown and gloves together, then hand antisepsis
Gloves, then gown, then hand antisepsis
questions.explanation: Surgical hand antisepsis is performed first, followed by drying, gowning, and then gloving.

questions.question: A patient's ulnar nerve is most vulnerable to compression injury when the arm is positioned:
choices: Abducted on an armboard at 45 degrees
Tucked at the side in pronation
Tucked at the side in supination
questions.explanation: Pronation of the tucked forearm places the cubital tunnel against the table surface, compressing the ulnar nerve; the neutral or supinated position is preferred.

questions.question: When a frozen section specimen is sent to pathology, how should it be sent?
choices: Frozen in dry ice at the field
questions.explanation: Frozen section specimens are sent fresh (without fixative) so the pathologist can freeze and examine the tissue for an immediate diagnosis.

questions.question: Which statement about the coagulation waveform compared to the cutting waveform is correct?
choices: The coagulation waveform is interrupted (modulated) and uses higher peak voltage
The cut waveform is intermittent and lower power
The coagulation waveform produces no heat
Both waveforms are identical in voltage
questions.explanation: The cutting waveform is a continuous low-voltage current, whereas the coagulation waveform is interrupted (modulated) with higher peak voltage, which favors hemostasis over vaporization.

questions.question: A new graduate nurse is assigned to circulate her first independent case. The most appropriate orientation practice is to:
choices: Have her circulate alone to build confidence
Pair her with a preceptor until competency is validated
Assign her only to scrub roles permanently
Document her as competent based on her degree
questions.explanation: Competency must be validated through a structured orientation and preceptorship before a nurse independently assumes a role; a degree alone does not establish role competency.

questions.question: When the scrub person sets up the instrument table, sharps and needles should be:
choices: Organized and contained in a designated area or device
questions.explanation: Containing sharps in a designated location, such as a needle counter or magnetic pad, supports accountability and reduces injury risk.

questions.question: If a sterile item is dropped onto a surface of questionable sterility, it should be:
choices: Used if it lands face up
Wiped and returned to the field
questions.explanation: An item that contacts a surface of questionable sterility is considered contaminated and must not be used on the sterile field.

questions.question: What is the recommended direction for applying a surgical prep at a clean surgical site?
choices: Randomly to cover the area quickly
From the periphery toward the incision site
From the incision site outward toward the periphery
questions.explanation: Prep is applied starting at the incision site and moving outward in a circular or back-and-forth motion toward the periphery, from clean to dirty.

questions.question: Which fixative is most commonly used for routine permanent histologic specimens?
questions.explanation: 10 percent neutral buffered formalin is the standard fixative for routine permanent histopathology specimens.

questions.question: When using the active electrode (Bovie pencil), where should it be placed when not in active use?
choices: In a clean, dry, insulated holster
On the back table near flammable prep
questions.explanation: An inactive active electrode should be kept in a clean, dry, nonconductive holster to prevent inadvertent activation that could ignite drapes or burn the patient or staff.

questions.question: Surgical scheduling should prioritize OR throughput in a way that:
choices: Never compromises patient safety or required resources
Always books the shortest cases first regardless of acuity
questions.explanation: Efficient scheduling improves throughput, but it must never compromise safety, adequate staffing, or availability of required equipment and instruments.

questions.question: Suture size designated as 5-0 compared with size 2-0 is:
questions.explanation: In the USP numbering system, more zeros indicate a smaller diameter, so 5-0 is finer than 2-0.

questions.question: The primary purpose of a microbial barrier in a surgical gown is to:
choices: Absorb all fluids onto the gown surface
Prevent the passage of microorganisms between sterile and nonsterile areas
questions.explanation: Surgical gowns serve as a barrier to minimize the passage of microorganisms between sterile and nonsterile areas, protecting both patient and team member.

questions.question: Maintaining intraoperative normothermia is defined as keeping the core temperature at or above:
questions.explanation: Normothermia is generally defined as a core temperature of 36 degrees C or higher; values below this represent unintended hypothermia.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of placing a specimen intended for frozen section into formalin?
choices: It has no effect on the result
It can render the tissue unsuitable for accurate frozen-section interpretation
questions.explanation: Formalin fixation alters the tissue and can make accurate frozen-section diagnosis impossible, so frozen sections must go fresh.

questions.question: A scenario reveals the dispersive pad was placed over a tattoo with heavy metallic ink. What is the best response?
choices: Remove all electrosurgery from the case
Proceed because tattoos do not affect conductivity
Relocate the pad to clean skin over well-vascularized tissue away from the tattoo if possible
questions.explanation: Heavy metallic pigment may alter conductivity and concentrate current; placing the pad over clean, well-vascularized skin away from such areas reduces burn risk.

questions.question: Competency validation in the perioperative setting is best demonstrated by:
